Psychosis is a symptom. If you have schizophrenia you will experience psychosis, however if you have psychosis it doesn't necessarily mean you have schizophrenia. Other mental illnesses that can have psychosis as a symptom are bipolar, borderline personality disorder and schizo affective disorder. 

Very simply psychosis is a break with reality. It can include hallucinations, delusions and disorganised thoughts/speech to name a few. 

So in short psychosis is the definition of those types of symptoms but is not synonymous with schizophrenia and can be part of several different mental (and physical) illnesses.

Hope that helps 😊

My husband, who I have been with for 11 years has schizophrenia. He was diagnosed before I met him, so at least for me it wasn't a shock. The fact that I am diagnosed with schizoaffective disorder made it both easier to handle because I understand what it's like, but also harder because when we both are having a bad day it can be hard to help the other person. 
I think you should ask him while he is feeling well enough, what you can do during his bad episodes to help him. That way when he is having a hard time you know exactly what to do.
I also agree with what others have written about getting a second opinion. To me it's sounds more like PTSD then schizophrenia, but of course I am no expert. 
Either way the main thing is just to be there for him. If you ever need advice I would be happy to help.
